scenarioStory.history: Roommate returned home to find the patient drowsy and confused on the couch, with an empty amitriptyline bottle on the coffee table that had roughly 30 pills two days ago. Roommate reports patient sent a concerning text message about an hour before being found and estimates she took the pills sometime in the last hour.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 34-year-old female with an intentional amitriptyline overdose approximately one hour ago, now drowsy, tachycardic, and hypotensive. → Monitor placed, widened QRS identified: Crew places the patient on a cardiac monitor with close attention to QRS duration given the known TCA ingestion, identifying a widened QRS consistent with sodium channel blockade, and establishes IV access. → Sodium bicarbonate given, QRS narrows: Sodium bicarbonate is administered for the widened QRS, and the crew reassesses to confirm the QRS is narrowing along with improving blood pressure, repeating the dose as needed. → QRS narrowed, stable for transport: The patient remains stable with a narrowed QRS and improving vital signs. The crew maintains continuous cardiac monitoring, patient safety precautions, and transports for definitive toxicology and psychiatric care.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Found by roommate after intentional overdose, empty pill bottle nearby

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 34-year-old female with an intentional amitriptyline overdose approximately one hour ago, now drowsy, tachycardic, and hypotensive.
relatedChecklist: Ensure scene and patient safety given the intentional, self-harm nature of the ingestion
Continuously monitor ECG with specific attention to QRS duration

scenarioEvents.name: Monitor placed, widened QRS identified
scenarioEvents.description: Crew places the patient on a cardiac monitor with close attention to QRS duration given the known TCA ingestion, identifying a widened QRS consistent with sodium channel blockade, and establishes IV access.
relatedChecklist: Sodium bicarbonate 65 mEq IV (65 kg × 1 mEq/kg), repeat as needed to narrow QRS and improve BP

scenarioEvents.name: Sodium bicarbonate given, QRS narrows
scenarioEvents.description: Sodium bicarbonate is administered for the widened QRS, and the crew reassesses to confirm the QRS is narrowing along with improving blood pressure, repeating the dose as needed.
relatedChecklist: Repeat vital signs and ECG frequently; monitor closely for rapid deterioration

scenarioEvents.name: QRS narrowed, stable for transport
scenarioEvents.description: The patient remains stable with a narrowed QRS and improving vital signs. The crew maintains continuous cardiac monitoring, patient safety precautions, and transports for definitive toxicology and psychiatric care.

scenarioEvents.name: Sodium bicarbonate withheld despite widened QRS
scenarioEvents.description: Sodium bicarbonate is not given despite the identified QRS widening. The cardiotoxicity progresses, with further QRS widening, worsening hypotension, and new seizure activity.
relatedChecklist: Give rescue sodium bicarbonate 65-130 mEq IV (65 kg × 1-2 mEq/kg) now for progressive QRS widening
Treat the seizure per the Seizures Guideline if it recurs or persists
